name: Narasimha Jayanthi
description: Festival celebrating the birth of Lord Narasimha at the nine-shrine Ahobilam temple complex in Nandyal, where mythology places the site of the deity's emergence from a pillar. Attracts thousands of devotees to this sacred Kshetra dedicated to the fierce lion-man avatar.
significance: Religious—avatar of Vishnu, supreme at this historic shrine

name: Maha Shivaratri
description: One of the major festivals at Amareswara Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva, drawing thousands of pilgrims to this Pancharama Kshetra on the Krishna River. Commemorates the cosmic dance and meditation of Lord Shiva.
significance: Religious—worship of Shiva; temple is one of five sacred Pancharama shrines

name: Belum Caves Festival
description: Kandanavolu Sambaralu—a two-day festival hosted by the Andhra Pradesh Government at India's second-longest open cave system. Features competitions (bullock-cart races, rangoli, cooking), traditional tribal dances, and cultural exhibitions celebrating the historic Buddhist/Jain cave heritage.
significance: Cultural—promotion of ancient cave heritage and Kurnool tribal traditions

name: Gandikota Festival
description: Annual celebration at the 1000-year-old Gandikota Fort showcasing the 300-foot Pennar Gorge. Features historical dramas, folk performances, magic shows, paragliding, helicopter rides (360° aerial views), boating, and local craft/food stalls celebrating Kandanavolu heritage.
significance: Cultural—preservation of 1000+ year fort heritage and regional folk traditions

name: Lepakshi Brahmotsavam (Maha Shivaratri)
description: 10-day annual Masi Brahmotsavam at the 16th-century Veerabhadra temple, climaxing with the spectacular car festival (Rathotsavam) where the deity's chariot is drawn through Lepakshi streets. Attracts thousands to this Vijayanagara architectural masterpiece.
significance: Religious—Brahmotsavam rituals honoring Lord Veerabhadra; cultural—traditional chariot procession

name: Shivratri Tribal Dance Mela
description: Annual tribal dance festival organized at this Eastern Ghats eco-tourism site where indigenous communities of the Maredumilli forest region celebrate with traditional Mela performances. Showcases tribal biodiversity and cultural heritage alongside forest conservation efforts.
significance: Cultural—preservation of tribal dance traditions; environmental—forest conservation celebration

name: Lumbini Festival
description: Three-day Buddhist cultural festival held at Nagarjuna Sagar Dam commemorating the significance of Buddhism in Andhra Pradesh (the state's dominant religion 2000 years ago). Features exhibitions of Buddhist art, local crafts, cultural shows, and spiritual activities celebrating the birthplace theme of Lord Buddha (Lumbini).
significance: Religious/Cultural—Buddhist heritage and meditation traditions; historical—ancient Buddhist center

name: Srivari Brahmotsavam
description: The largest and most significant annual festival at Lord Venkateswara Temple in Tirumala-Tirupati. Nine-day celebration featuring daily processional vahanas (chariots) with the deity and consorts Sridevi/Bhudevi, culminating in spectacular chariot processions through temple streets. Attracts pilgrims globally.
significance: Religious—Brahma's cleansing ceremony; one of Hinduism's premier Vaishnavite festivals

name: Reh Festival
description: The Reh Festival is the most significant cultural celebration of the Idu Mishmi community, marking ritual propitiation of deities and thanksgiving for harmony, health, and prosperity. The festival features traditional dances, elaborate handwoven attire adorned with bright patterns, and ancient ceremonial practices rooted in the tribe's spiritual connection with ancestral beliefs.
significance: Tribal religious observance; harvest and prosperity blessing for the Idu Mishmi people

name: Podi-Barbi Festival
description: Podi-Barbi is a harvest festival celebrated by the Ramo, Pai-Libo, and Bokar communities (Adi subtribes) of Mechuka, serving as thanksgiving to Mother Nature for agricultural abundance. The festival features traditional competitions (archery, wrestling, tug-of-war), the Yapung ceremony where rice beer is exchanged as a symbol of friendship and goodwill, and community feasting that strengthens social bonds.
significance: Agricultural harvest blessing; community thanksgiving and social harmony for the Adi people

name: Solung Festival
description: Solung is the most significant socio-religious festival for the Adi community in Pasighat, marking the completion of crop sowing and transplanting. The five-day celebration features the Ponung dance performed by women of all ages, animal sacrifices to appease agricultural deities, traditional weapon crafting, narrative songs honouring ancestral stories, and community feasts with locally brewed rice beer shared as a gesture of unity.
significance: Agricultural festival; ancestral propitiation and harvest blessing for the Adi people

name: Raas Mahotsav
description: A grand theatrical celebration held across 65+ satras of Majuli, showcasing Raas Leela performances that depict Lord Krishna's divine life through Bhaonas (religious plays). Dancers, musicians, and actors from the satras perform with traditional instruments, masks, and artistic costumes, attracting hundreds of thousands of devotees and visitors who are hosted by local families during the 4-5 day festival.
significance: Religious and cultural significance for Vaishnavite tradition; Majuli is the pre-eminent venue for this 180+ year theatrical tradition, first performed at Dakhinpat Satra in 1840 AD

name: Kaziranga Elephant Festival
description: A celebration of wildlife conservation and cultural heritage held at Kaziranga National Park, featuring hundreds of decorated Asiatic elephants in parades, races, football matches, and dance performances. Jointly organized by Assam's Forest and Tourism Departments to highlight elephant conservation efforts and address human-wildlife conflict mitigation.
significance: Conservation awareness for endangered one-horned Asian elephant; celebration of the park's global wildlife importance

name: Assam Spring Festival
description: A two-day cultural celebration held at Manas National Park showcasing local food, traditional handloom and handicrafts of Bodo communities living around the park. The festival promotes alternative livelihoods for fringe villagers while celebrating the cultural diversity of Bodoland in the biodiversity-rich environment of a UNESCO World Heritage site.
significance: Cultural and economic significance for indigenous Bodo community; celebration of tribal traditions within a global wildlife conservation context

name: Nirvana Mahotsav
description: An annual Jain pilgrimage celebration commemorating Lord Mahavira's attainment of Nirvana at Pawapuri on the night of Diwali. Devotees gather to participate in religious ceremonies and rituals at the Jal Mandir (water temple), including the offering of a 151-kilogram blessed laddu to Lord Mahavira and its distribution among thousands of pilgrims.
significance: Sacred to Jainism; Pawapuri is Mahavira's nirvana site, the most important pilgrimage destination for Jain commemoration of the faith's founder

name: Vaishali Mahotsav
description: A significant Jain festival celebrated at Vaishali, the birthplace of Lord Mahavira, featuring grand chariot processions with Mahavir images, religious ceremonies in temples, fasting, charitable donations, and devotional scripture readings. Both Digambara and Shwetambara Jain communities participate in this major pilgrimage festival.
significance: Religious and pilgrimage significance for Jainism; Vaishali is the birthplace of the 24th Tirthankara (spiritual leader) and a major Buddhist pilgrimage site as well, making it a shared sacred destination

name: Bhoramdeo Mahotsav
description: Annual festival dedicated to Lord Shiva at Bhoramdeo Temple. Features traditional folk dances, music, theatrical presentations, and tribal crafts. Local tribes and artisans participate, showcasing handwoven textiles, pottery, and tribal jewelry.
significance: Celebrates the rich cultural and religious heritage of Khajuraho-style temple and tribal traditions of Chhattisgarh.

name: Sirpur Mahotsav (National Dance and Music Festival)
description: Annual national-level festival held at the backdrop of 7th-century Lakshmana Temple and Mahanadi River banks. Features classical, folk, and tribal dance performances from across India, including Panthi, Danda, and Bastariya dances, alongside music by national and international artists.
significance: Celebrates Sirpur's archaeological and Buddhist-Hindu heritage while promoting classical arts and local tribal culture.

name: Sarhul
approximate_date: March–April (Chaitra Shukla Paksha, 3rd day to Purnima)
description: Spring festival marking the tribal new year, celebrated primarily by Oraon, Munda, and Ho tribes. Involves worship of the Sal tree (abode of Sarna Maa) with offerings of flowers, fruits, vermilion, and rooster. Processions organized in Ranchi since 1961; features traditional dances with Sal flowers.
significance: Symbolizes the marriage of Earth and Sun; marks the beginning of the agricultural season and the tribal year. Emphasizes tribal identity and social justice.

name: Sammed Shikhar Festival
description: Annual fair at Shikharji (Sammed Shikhar, Parasnath Hill) drawing large numbers of Jain devotees. Pilgrims ascend the sacred hill to visit 20+ temples and shrines commemorating the 20 Tirthankaras who attained nirvana here.
significance: Major Jain pilgrimage site and annual fair; spiritually significant for Jain devotees seeking religious merit and pilgrimage experience.

name: Mahavir Jayanti
description: Birth anniversary of Lord Mahavir, the 24th Tirthankara. At Shikharji, devotees participate in processions, scripture recitations, and charitable meals. Pilgrimage to Shikharji is particularly significant during this festival.
significance: Most important festival for Jain community; commemorates the spiritual teachings and liberation of Lord Mahavir.

name: Goa Carnival
description: Goa's largest carnival parade, with Margao hosting vibrant celebrations on February 15. The parade moves from Holy Spirit Church to Margao Municipal Council Square, featuring elaborate floats, dance groups, drummers, and live music in South Goa's main city.
significance: Christian cultural festival celebrating pre-Lenten traditions

name: Shigmo (Shigmotsav)
description: Goa's major spring harvest festival with large parade in Margao on March 14. Hundreds of folk artists perform traditional dances like Ghode Mhodni and Romtamel while massive Chitrarath floats depicting scenes from Hindu epics roll through the city centre.
significance: Hindu spring festival rooted in Phalguna month, celebrating harvest and renewal

name: Feast of the Three Kings (Reis Magos)
description: The Chapel of Nossa Senhora dos Remédios (Our Lady of Cures), also known as the Three Kings Chapel, atop the Cuelim hillock near Reis Magos, hosts the most famous celebration. Three young boys enact the role of the Three Kings, traveling on horseback through different paths and converging near the chapel.
significance: Christian religious festival commemorating the visit of the Three Wise Men to Bethlehem

name: Sao Joao Festival (São João)
description: Siolim hosts a distinctive 175-year-old boat festival tradition where revellers from surrounding villages (Chapora, Zhor, Badem, Assagao) arrive in beautifully decorated boats to pay homage at the Chapel of São João in Pereira Vaddo. Boats are decorated with flowers, leaves, and designs of guitars, birds, fruit baskets, sea creatures, and mythical creatures. Festival begins at 3:30 PM with boats arriving between 4 PM and 5:30 PM.
significance: Catholic religious festival celebrating St. John the Baptist, merged with monsoon and community traditions

name: Sao Joao Festival (São João)
description: Sao Joao is celebrated across North Goa, with significant traditions in Assagao. Revellers from Badem in Assagao join other villages in the famous boat procession to Siolim's Chapel of São João, connecting Assagao's Catholic heritage with this major monsoon celebration.
significance: Catholic religious festival celebrating St. John the Baptist, merged with monsoon and community traditions

name: Shigmo (Shigmotsav)
description: Ponda marks the official start of Shigmotsav on March 5, 2026. Local Hindu temples including Shantadurga Temple, Mangeshi Temple (in nearby Priol), and Mahalsa Temple (in Mardol) host celebrations with folk artists performing traditional dances and farmers gathering for rituals, folk songs, and community feasts.
significance: Hindu spring festival rooted in Phalguna month, celebrating harvest and renewal with temple-centered traditions

name: Shantadurga Temple Annual Fair
description: The Shri Shantadurga Temple in Ponda, an 18th-century sanctuary dedicated to Goddess Durga, hosts an annual fair during December-January. The temple exhibits Indo-Portuguese architectural styles and is a major spiritual landmark in central Goa's Hindu heartland.
significance: Hindu religious festival at a major goddess temple celebrating devotional traditions

name: Mahalsa Temple Annual Jatra
description: The Shri Mahalsa Narayani Temple in Mardol, near Ponda, hosts an annual Jatra (festival) dedicated to Goddess Mahalasa (an incarnation of Lord Vishnu). The celebration features elaborate rituals, cultural programs, and processions that draw crowds from various parts of Goa.
significance: Hindu religious festival celebrating goddess traditions with community processions

name: Bhadarvi Poonam Mela
approximate_date: September (Bhadarvi Poonam full moon, typically early September)
description: A major pilgrimage fair at Ambaji temple, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, attracting hundreds of thousands of devotees during the full moon of Bhadrapad month. The fair features devotional rituals, folk music, Garba performances, and in recent years, grand drone light shows.
significance: Sacred Shakti Peeth pilgrimage; harvest moon spiritual celebration

name: Janmashtami Festival
description: Ranchhodrai temple in Dakor celebrates Lord Krishna's birthday with elaborate rituals, special prayers, colorful decorations, and traditional dances depicting scenes from Krishna's life. Thousands of devotees gather for special darshan.
significance: Lord Krishna birth anniversary; divine incarnation celebration

name: Sharad Purnima Festival
approximate_date: October (Sharad Purnima full moon, typically mid-October)
description: Celebrated as the day when Lord Krishna appears as Ranchodrai at Dakor temple. Elaborate processions with temple idols, cultural performances, and rituals commemorate the divine love of Radha and Krishna. Thousands of pilgrims gather for special celebrations.
significance: Radha-Krishna divine love celebration; autumn full moon festival

name: Bhavnath Mela (Girnar Mahashivratri Mela)
description: A five-day sacred fair at the Bhavnath Mahadev temple at the foothills of Girnar mountain, honoring Lord Shiva. The fair is renowned for processions of naga sadhus, ritual bathing in holy Mrugi Kund, devotional singing through the night, and traditional bhavai folk dances. Attracts thousands of pilgrims and ascetics.
significance: Lord Shiva veneration; major pilgrimage and ashram gathering

name: Uttarardh Mahotsav (Modhera Dance Festival)
description: A two-day classical dance festival celebrating the winter solstice at the ancient Sun Temple. The festival showcases diverse Indian classical dance forms including Odissi, Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Manipuri, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, and Sattriya. Named after the astronomical halfway point of the sun's northward journey, honoring the sun god.
significance: Celebration of classical arts and solar astronomy

name: Mandvi Beach Festival
description: A ten-day coastal cultural festival at Mandvi Beach with free entry, featuring nightly cultural musical performances with renowned artists on weekends. The festival includes adventure activities, beach sports, sand art, bonfire arrangements, live music, stargazing sessions, laser light shows, and traditional craft and food stalls against the Arabian Sea backdrop.
significance: Coastal cultural celebration; year-end festive gathering

name: Dholavira Festival
approximate_date: Varies (cultural heritage festival, dates to be announced)
description: A heritage festival blending archaeology with contemporary performance at India's oldest urban site. Features interactive heritage walks through the Harappan city layout, traditional crafts demonstrations including block printing and bead making, and performances by folk and classical musicians. Free entry for all visitors, promoting heritage-based tourism and archaeological education.
significance: Archaeological heritage celebration; Harappan civilization education

name: Lili Parikrama (Green Circumambulation of Mount Girnar)
approximate_date: Kartik Sud Agyaras to Kartik Sud Poonam
description: A sacred pilgrimage circumambulating Mount Girnar during the Hindu month of Kartik. The green parikrama (pradakshina) is approximately 36 km through dense forest, starting from Bhavnath temple. Around 1 lakh pilgrims participate, walking over 4 days, honoring Girnar as a sacred peak for both Hindu and Jain faiths.
significance: Major pilgrimage for Hindus (reverence for Lord Dattatreya and other deities) and Jains (sacred site of Neminath, the 22nd Tirthankara). Girnar is believed to be one of the oldest and most sacred mountains in India.

name: Bhavnath Maha Shivaratri Mela
description: A 5-day fair held at the Bhavnath Mahadev Temple at the foothills of Mount Girnar near Junagadh. The festival culminates on the auspicious night of Maha Shivaratri when devotees believe Lord Shiva himself visits the temple. Naga Sadhus arrive in grand processions on elephants, blowing conch shells and chanting hymns. Grand puja of Lord Shiva is conducted at midnight.
significance: Ancient festival with thousands of pilgrims, saints, and devotees from across India gathering to participate in rituals dedicated to Lord Shiva. Features traditional folk music, dances, and tribal participation.

name: Gandhi Jayanti Celebrations at Kirti Mandir
description: Annual celebration of Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary at Kirti Mandir, his ancestral home and birthplace in Porbandar. Official ceremonies include wreaths, speeches honoring Gandhi as the Father of the Nation, and cultural exhibitions of rare photographs, manuscripts, and memorabilia related to his life and work.
significance: Porbandar is Gandhi's birthplace, making this destination iconic for Gandhi Jayanti. The celebration emphasizes Gandhi's teachings of non-violence, peace, and service. Attended by state officials and spiritual leaders.

name: Water Festival - Rani ki Vav
description: Annual cultural festival organized by the Government of Gujarat to celebrate the grandeur of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Rani ki Vav stepwell in Patan. Features classical and folk dance performances including Garba, Raas, and Bharatanatyam. The stepwell is beautifully illuminated at night. Includes handicraft exhibitions highlighting Patan's famous Patola sarees, heritage walks, and traditional Gujarati food stalls.
significance: Celebrates the 11th-century architectural masterpiece built by Queen Udayamati. Honors Patan's rich cultural heritage and brings together visitors and locals to experience the monument's intricate carvings and historical importance.

name: Saputara Monsoon Festival
description: Annual festival organized by the Gujarat Tourism Department to celebrate tribal culture and the natural beauty of the Saputara region in the Dang District. Features tribal food festival, tattoo workshop, art & craft stalls, tribal costume photoshoot, folk fusion concerts, Warli painting workshop, and performances by over 350 folk artists. First week themed 'Tribal Heritage Week' showcasing tribal arts, crafts, traditional cuisines, and exhibitions of tribal skills.
significance: Celebrates the rich cultural heritage of tribal communities including Kunbis, Bhils, Gamits, and Warlis. Promotes local traditions, folk arts, and the region's unique tribal identity. Major platform for cultural exchange and tourism promotion.

name: Dang Darbar Festival
approximate_date: February-March (historically before Holi; 2026 dates: Feb 26 - Mar 3)
description: One of Gujarat's most significant tribal festivals held in Ahwa, Dang District, in the Saputara Hills. Gatherings of diverse tribal communities including Bhils, Kunbis, Warlis, and Gamits in traditional attire. Spectacular tribal dances performed in concentric circles with traditional percussion and wind instruments (Kahalia, Tadpur). The festival's name was changed to 'Jamabandi Durbar' with the District Collector officiating.
significance: Historic festival with origins dating to 1842, when an agreement was reached between the British East India Company and five tribal kings (Gadhavi, Pimpri, Amala-Linga, Vasurana, Daher). Celebrates tribal culture, dance, music, and community traditions of the Dang region.

name: Losar (Tibetan New Year)
description: Three-day Tibetan New Year celebration marking the Fire Horse Year (2026). Families prepare khapse (traditional Tibetan sweets), monasteries conduct prayers, and thousands gather at Tsuglagkhang temple. Dalai Lama participates in celebrations.
significance: Major religious and cultural festival for the Tibetan exile community in McLeod Ganj, central to Buddhist practice and annual renewal.

name: Dalai Lama's Birthday
description: Celebration of His Holiness the Dalai Lama's birthday, featuring prayers and cultural events at Tsuglagkhang temple and surrounding areas. Monastics from all traditions, dignitaries, and Buddhist practitioners gather for ceremonies.
significance: Significant religious observance for the Tibetan Buddhist community, marking the 90th birthday (2026) with special significance.

name: Manimahesh Yatra
approximate_date: August 16 - September 19 (Janmashtami to Radha Ashtami, lunar calendar)
description: Sacred pilgrimage to Manimahesh Lake (4,080m) at the foot of Mount Kailash in Bharmour region, coinciding with Krishna Janmashtami. Thousands of devotees trek to the holy lake. Bharmour hosts a fair with local customs and rituals.
significance: One of the major Hindu pilgrimages in Himachal Pradesh, held on the sacred lunar calendar tied to Krishna's birth, attracting devotees region-wide.

name: Shrikhand Mahadev Yatra
description: Sacred pilgrimage to Shrikhand Mahadev peak (18,570m) featuring a naturally formed 75-foot Shivling. One of the most challenging treks in India, organized by Kullu District Administration during the Shravan month (auspicious for Shiva worship). Base camps with facilities at five locations.
significance: Panch Kailash shrine, considered one of the toughest pilgrimages in India. Shravan is the most sacred month for Shiva worship in Hindu tradition.

name: Kinner Kailash Parikrama
description: 60 km sacred pilgrimage circuit around Kinner Kailash peak in Kinnaur, with a naturally formed 79-foot Shivling at 4,400m. Trek starts from Charang village and ends at Chitkul in Baspa Valley. Believed to grant spiritual liberation through karmic purification.
significance: Sacred circumambulation (parikrama) of the peak believed to be Lord Shiva's divine dwelling place. Central to regional Hindu spirituality.

name: Phulaich (Festival of Flowers)
description: Festival celebrating wildflower blooms in upper Kinnaur, featuring processions of local deities, traditional folk dances, and reenactments of ancient war scenes in traditional attire. Three-day 'Ukhyang' celebration at Sangla Valley organized by Kinnaur administration.
significance: Tribal harvest festival of the Kinnaura people, celebrating the bond between community and nature. Central to local cultural identity.

name: Prashar Mela (Parashar Fair)
description: Annual fair at the 13th-century Parashar Rishi Temple on the shores of Prashar Lake (2,730m) in Mandi district. Devta processions where idols of regional deities are carried in traditional sedans by foot. Includes folk music and local cuisine.
significance: Regional pilgrimage fair dedicated to Sage Parashar, attracting devotees from neighboring valleys. Important cultural gathering for mountain communities.

name: Minjar Fair
description: Major Chamba district fair held at Chaugan ground celebrating the harvest season. Farming community offers first corn silk ('Minjar') to River Ravi for good harvests. Features stalls selling local crafts and produce, with evening cultural performances.
significance: Agricultural festival central to farming communities in Chamba, held across the region including Dalhousie area, representing gratitude for nature's bounty.

name: Losar (Tibetan New Year / Halda)
description: Buddhist new year celebration in Lahaul known locally as 'Halda', marking the end of harvest season. Monasteries perform ritual 'Cham dances' (masked devil dances) in colorful costumes depicting triumph of good over evil. Includes traditional Tibetan Buddhist ceremonies.
significance: Sacred renewal festival for Buddhist communities in the high Himalayan valleys, central to regional spiritual practice.

name: Fagli Festival
approximate_date: March (Amavasya/moonless night, aligned with Basant Panchami)
description: Traditional tribal festival in Yangpa village and Tirthan Valley marking the end of winter and victory of good over evil. Men in traditional masks dance in circles while locals gather. Arrow shooting at Ravana portraits occurs in some villages during Basant Panchami.
significance: Ancient tribal celebration of seasonal transition and spiritual purification unique to Kinnaur district communities.

name: Navratri Pilgrimage at Vaishno Devi
description: Massive pilgrimage surge at Mata Vaishno Devi shrine during the nine-day Navratri festival. The shrine area is decorated with vibrant floral arrangements and colorful lights. Special Maha Yagya ceremonies with Vedic hymns are performed. Attracts hundreds of thousands of devotees during both Chaitra Navratri (Mar-Apr) and Sharad Navratri (Sep-Oct).
significance: One of the most significant Hindu pilgrimage festivals in India. Vaishno Devi is one of the 51 Shakti Peeths. Pilgrims trek to the cave shrine 5,200 ft above Katra town.

name: Lolab Winter Festival
description: A two-day celebration of Kashmiri culture held at Kariwan in Devar Lolab. Features traditional folk music, snow volleyball, skiing, dance performances, local handicraft displays, and culinary delights. Attracts thousands of visitors for music performances, heritage walks, and nature experiences.
significance: Celebrates winter season and showcases scenic splendor of Lolab Valley. Promotes Lolab as a premier winter-tourism destination and generates economic activity for local businesses.

name: Likir Dosmochey (Stromochey) Festival
description: One of the most important monastic festivals in Ladakh held at Likir Monastery. Features vibrant masked dances (Cham) performed by monks in elaborate costumes depicting the triumph of good over evil. Sacred rituals and votive offerings (Dosmochey) are performed to ward off evil spirits.
significance: Marks the end of the harsh winter season and Tibetan New Year celebrations. Celebrates the Gelugpa Buddhist tradition at Likir, one of the major gompa festivals in Ladakh. Named the Festival of the Scapegoat.

name: Nowruz (Balti New Year)
description: Balti New Year celebration marked by special dishes, egg painting, egg fights, singing, dancing around fires, and traditional music. Believed that the winner of the egg fight will have good luck during the year.
significance: Ancient Persian-Balti spring festival celebrating renewal and prosperity. Unique to the Balti community in Turtuk, reflecting their historical cultural connections beyond the Indian border.

name: Champa Shashti (Shasti)
description: Major festival at Kukke Subramanya temple dedicated to Lord Subramanya (serpent deity). Champa Shashti celebrates the temple's primary festival observance, honoring both the deity and the serpent mythology central to this sacred site.
significance: Hindu religious festival celebrating Lord Subramanya and serpent worship traditions at a major Naga temple

name: Nagara Panchami
description: Festival celebrating serpent worship at Kukke Subramanya temple. Devotees perform rituals and pujas honoring snakes and seeking protection from snake-related dangers, central to this temple's spiritual significance.
significance: Hindu festival dedicated to serpent worship and protection rituals at the Kukke Subramanya temple

name: Ashlesha Bali Puja
approximate_date: Celebrated on specific lunar dates (Ashlesha Nakshatra)
description: One of the two most popular puja rituals conducted at Kukke Subramanya temple, specifically seeking protection from snakes and removal of snake-related curses through devotional ritual.
significance: Hindu religious ritual dedicated to serpent protection and spiritual remedies for snake-related fears

name: Khwaja Bande Nawaz Urs
approximate_date: 15-17 Dhu al-Qadah (Islamic lunar calendar, varies: typically August-September)
description: Death anniversary celebration (urs) of the revered Sufi saint Khwaja Bande Nawaz (1321-1422) at his mausoleum in Gulbarga (Kalaburagi). Thousands of devotees and pilgrims from various faiths gather over three days to seek spiritual blessings and participate in devotional observances.
significance: Sufi Islamic festival celebrating the death anniversary of a beloved saint, attended by people of multiple faiths

name: Karavali Utsav
description: Annual multi-day coastal cultural festival held at Rabindranath Tagore Beach in Karwar, celebrating the rich dance, music, culture, and natural heritage of the Karavali (coastal) region. Features performances by renowned artists, morning cultural programs, kite festivals, and various coastal celebrations.
significance: Regional coastal cultural festival celebrating Uttara Kannada's unique heritage and contemporary cultural expressions

name: Mandala-Makaravilakku Pilgrimage Season
description: The major 41-day pilgrimage season at Sabarimala Ayyappa Temple begins in early November (Vrishchikam Malayalam month) and culminates in mid-January (Makarasankranthi). The Mandala Pooja marks the midpoint, while Makaravilakku (lighting of the sacred lamp at nearby Ponnambalamedu) signals the season's end. Hundreds of thousands of devotees undertake this sacred pilgrimage.
significance: Principal annual pilgrimage season for devotees of Lord Ayyappa; represents devotional unity and penitential spiritual practice.

name: Cherai Pooram (Gowreeswara Temple Festival)
approximate_date: Late January to early February; Pooram Nakshatra day (Makaram month)
description: Annual festival at the 1912-built Gowreeswara Temple (also called South Pazhani) featuring Kavadi Utsavam honoring Lord Subramanian and the spectacular Pooram procession. The festival showcases 20–30 caparisoned elephants with gold-plated caparisons, decorated with bells and necklaces. Traditional offering: Ilaneer abhishekam (tender coconut ablution). Concludes with Arattu (ritual bathing of the deity).
significance: Iconic temple festival in Kerala featuring grand elephant processions and traditional religious ceremonies.

name: Marari Mahadeva Arattu (Temple Festival)
approximate_date: Kumbham month (February–March); Arattu on new moon day (10-day festival period ending)
description: Annual 10-day festival at the 700-year-old Mararikulam Sree Mahadeva Temple (one of India's oldest, uniquely depicting Mahadevan and Parvathi face-to-face). Festival commences with flag hoisting 10 days before Arattu. Features traditional Kerala performing arts (Kathakali, Chakyar Koothu, Nangyar Kooth), melam music, fireworks, and caparisoned elephants. Concludes with Arattu—ritual bathing of the deity in the sea.
significance: Major Shaivite pilgrimage festival showcasing classical Kerala temple traditions and ceremonies.

name: Thangal Para Uroos (Sufi Pilgrimage Festival)
description: Annual Urs (pilgrimage) festival at Thangal Para, a Muslim pilgrimage centre 5 km from Vagamon at 2,500m elevation. Honors Sheikh Fariduddin, a revered 13th-century Sufi saint from Afghanistan. Thousands of devotees gather on this sacred day to offer prayers. Traditional sweet dish Ganjusakkar is made and distributed to all attendees.
significance: Important Muslim pilgrimage festival celebrating Sufi spiritual heritage; unique syncretic interfaith sacred site in the Western Ghats.

name: Kartik Purnima
approximate_date: November (full moon day in Kartik month)
description: A significant Shiva festival celebrated at the Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga temple, commemorating the slaying of the demon Tripurasura by Lord Shiva. Celebrated on the full moon of the Kartik month with special rituals, prayers, and illuminations.
significance: Religious — marks a pivotal mythological event; major pilgrimage occasion

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
approximate_date: August–September (Shukla Chaturthi; 10-day festival ending on Anant Chaturdashi)
description: The Astavinayak Circuit's signature festival, celebrating the birth of Lord Ganesha across eight sacred temples (Ojhar, Morgaon, Theur, Ranjangaon, Siddhatek, Lenyadri, Mahad, Pali). This ancient 8-temple pilgrimage is most crowded during this 10-day festival when devotees visit all temples for darshan and special pujas.
significance: Religious—deity birth celebration; cultural—iconic Marathi festival; pilgrimage circuit is destination-defining

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: The grand celebration at the 400-year-old Swayambhu Ganapati Temple, one of Maharashtra's most sacred Ganpati shrines. Devotees perform pujas on the golden sands with the Arabian Sea as backdrop, attend aartis, and participate in the traditional Ganpati visarjan procession around the coastal town.
significance: Religious—deity birth celebration at famous self-manifested shrine; cultural—iconic Konkan coastal festival

name: Maha Shivaratri
approximate_date: February–March (14th lunar day of Phalgun month)
description: A major festival at the Harihareshwar Temple (also called Dakshin Kashi), where Lord Shiva is worshipped with elaborate aarti ceremonies, processions, and sacred hymns. Attracts large crowds of devotees to this ancestral Peshwa temple on the Konkan coast.
significance: Religious—deity worship; pilgrimage—temple is regarded as the Kashi of the South

name: Ellora-Ajanta Festival
description: An annual cultural festival at the UNESCO World Heritage Ellora Caves site celebrating Indian classical art, music, and dance. Features Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, and Kuchipudi performances, along with Hindustani and Carnatic music concerts against the backdrop of the ancient rock-cut monuments.
significance: Cultural heritage—celebrates India's classical traditions at an ancient UNESCO site

name: Monsoon Festival
description: A festival celebrating Amboli's lush monsoon landscape in the Western Ghats. Features guided nature tours, butterfly watching, birding expeditions, amphibian and reptile exploration, and nature camps showcasing the region's rich biodiversity during peak rainfall season.
significance: Eco-tourism—celebrates monsoon ecology and biodiversity; natural heritage

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: The primary festival at the Girijatmaj Ashtavinayak temple, celebrating Lord Ganesha's birth. Girijatmaj means 'son of Parvati' — legend holds the goddess meditated 12 years in Lenyadri for Ganesha's birth, and he grew there for 15 years. The temple, carved into the mountain cave, hosts elaborate pujas, abhishek (ritual bath), and aartis attracting pilgrims from across Maharashtra to this sacred Ashtavinayak shrine.
significance: Religious—deity birth celebration; pilgrimage—Lenyadri is one of eight Ashtavinayak temples (the only cave-based shrine in the circuit)

name: Maghi Ganesh Jayanti
description: A secondary but significant festival celebrating the rebirth/reappearance of Lord Ganesha in the Magh month. Marks another sacred occasion for the Ashtavinayak circuit, with special pujas and temple rituals.
significance: Religious—deity celebration; pilgrimage occasion at the sacred cave temple

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: The signature festival at Morgaon's Mayureshwar (Moreshwar) temple, the first of the eight Ashtavinayak shrines. The festival features elaborate rituals, abhishek (ritual bathing of the idol), maha-aarti ceremonies, bhajans, and kirtans. Thousands of devotees throng the temple seeking Ganesha's blessings, and the atmosphere is filled with devotion and celebration. Morgaon village's name itself means 'village of peacocks,' reflecting its sacred status.
significance: Religious—deity birth celebration; pilgrimage—Morgaon marks the start of the historic Ashtavinayak Yatra circuit

name: Maghi Ganesh Jayanti
description: Celebrates the birth/reappearance of Lord Ganesha in the Magh month. The festival includes special pujas, recitation of Ganesh Stotras (hymns), and deepdan (lighting of sacred lamps) at the Mayureshwar temple, drawing devotees across the Ashtavinayak circuit.
significance: Religious—deity celebration; pilgrimage occasion

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: The major festival at the Varadvinayak Ashtavinayak temple in Mahad, celebrating Lord Ganesha's birth. The temple features elaborate ceremonies including pranpratistha (idol consecration), abhishek (ritual bathing), and special pujas. The temple's swayambhu (self-manifested) idol is said to have been discovered in an adjacent lake in 1690, and an oil lamp in the shrine has been burning continuously since 1892. Thousands of devotees visit during the 10-day festival.
significance: Religious—deity birth celebration; pilgrimage—one of the eight Ashtavinayak temples with a legendary self-manifested idol

name: Maghi Ganesh Jayanti
description: Honors the birth/reappearance of Ganesha in the Magh month with special pujas, havans (fire rituals), recitation of sacred hymns, and a grand maha-aarti at the Varadvinayak temple.
significance: Religious—deity celebration; pilgrimage occasion at the Ashtavinayak shrine

name: Navratri
approximate_date: September–October (Shukla Paksha, Pratipada to Dashami; 9–10 days)
description: The major festival at the Ekvira Aai Devi temple at Karla Caves, celebrating the Goddess Durga. The Ekvira is the Kuladevi (clan deity) of the Koli fishing community and is also worshipped by the Chandraseniya Kayastha Prabhu community. The festival features chaturdashi baths (ritual bathing), folk songs, processions, and grand celebrations. Every year, Kolis pay respect to Ekvira and celebrate the festival with traditional rituals.
significance: Religious—goddess worship; cultural—iconic festival of the Koli community; the only temple in India with a shrine to the sacred Shami tree

name: Dussehra (Seemollanghan at Shami Tree)
description: The Ekvira Devi temple at Karla is unique—it is the only temple in India with a shrine dedicated to the sacred Shami tree, attracting thousands of devotees for Seemollanghan (leaf-exchange ritual) on Dussehra. This ancient tradition involves exchanging Shami leaves as a symbol of victory and prosperity.
significance: Religious—sacred tree worship and Dussehra celebration; cultural—unique to this temple

name: Kamala Devi Festival
description: A pilgrimage festival centered on the Kamalja (Kamala) Devi Temple near Lonar Crater Lake. The crater's sacred temples, dating back to the 6th century, draw devotees throughout the year. Large numbers of pilgrims visit during the festival, believing the lake to be sacred and that Lord Vishnu created it to preserve the universe. The Daitya Sudan Temple (built in Hemadpanti style) and Gomukh Temple (with a perennial stream flowing from a cow-shaped rock carving) are also active pilgrimage sites.
significance: Religious—goddess worship and sacred lake pilgrimage; geological—unique 52,000-year-old meteorite crater surrounded by temples

name: Krishnabai Annual Utsav
description: The major festival at the Krishnabai Temple (also called Krishna Devi Temple) in Old Mahabaleshwar, celebrating the birthplace of the perennial Krishna River. The temple is the source of the sacred river, and the Utsav marks the spiritual bond between the goddess and the river's origin. The festival begins on Purnima Tithi (full moon) and attracts pilgrims from across the region.
significance: Religious—goddess and river-source worship; geographical—marks the origin of the Krishna River, one of India's major waterways

name: Dhammachakra Pravartan Din
description: Annual observance commemorating the historic mass conversion to Buddhism led by B. R. Ambedkar on October 14-15, 1956 at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur, when approximately 600,000 Dalits renounced Hinduism and embraced Buddhism. Celebrations feature processions with Ambedkar's blue flag and Buddha statues, conversion ceremonies, cultural programs, bhajans, and seminars.
significance: Landmark Buddhist festival; celebrates Ambedkarite Buddhism and social equality; up to 70,000 new converts annually.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: Celebrated at Vighnahar Ganapati Temple, one of the eight Ashtavinayak temples. Birth anniversary of Lord Ganesha with temple decorations, processions, and devotional rituals.
significance: Major Ashtavinayak pilgrimage festival; temple renovated by Peshwa-era leader Chimaji Appa.

name: Maghi Ganesh (Maghi Chaturthi)
description: Festival celebrating Lord Ganesha in the month of Magh (January-February) at Vighnahar Ganapati Temple.
significance: Secondary Ashtavinayak festival; Magh month observance.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: Grand celebration at Ballaleshwar Ganpati Temple, one of the eight Ashtavinayak temples.
significance: Ashtavinayak festival; temple unique as only Ganesha incarnation known by devotee's name (Ballala).

name: Maghi Utsav (Magha Chaturthi)
description: Celebrated January-February at Ballaleshwar temple with rituals, devotional singing, bhajans, and kirtans.
significance: Major Ashtavinayak festival; temple features Vinayaka idol with two diamonds in eyes.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: Grand celebration at Mahaganapati Temple, one of the eight Ashtavinayak temples believed to house the most powerful form of Ganesha.
significance: Ashtavinayak pilgrimage festival; temple dates to 9th-10th centuries.

name: Ganesh Jayanti (Maghi)
description: Festival celebrating rebirth of Lord Ganesha in Magha (January-February) with aartis, bhajans, and processions.
significance: Ashtavinayak festival period; marks Ganesha rebirth.

name: Ram Navami
description: Celebrated as Lord Rama's birth. Sai Baba encouraged its celebration in 1911, uniting Hindu and Muslim communities. Processions, puja, music, and public parayana.
significance: One of three major Shirdi Sai Baba temple festivals; represents Sai Baba's inclusive spiritual philosophy.

name: Guru Purnima
description: The only festival Sai Baba explicitly asked his devotees to celebrate. Honors spiritual gurus with puja, bhajan, parayana, and processions.
significance: Sai Baba-mandated festival; honors spiritual teachers and Sai Baba's guruship; records highest attendance in India.

name: Vijayadashami (Sai Baba Punyatithi)
description: Marks Sai Baba's Mahasamadhi (death) on October 15, 1918. Observed with puja, bhajan, parayana, and exuberant processions.
significance: Sai Baba's death anniversary; considered holy day; one of three major temple festivals.

name: Ganesh Jayanti (Maghi Ganesh)
description: Celebrated in Magha (January-February) at Siddhivinayak Temple, marking Ganesha's rebirth. Three-day palkhi (palanquin) procession with devotional singing.
significance: Ashtavinayak festival; temple has unique eastern-facing idol with trunk turned right, symbolizing supreme spiritual energy.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: Grand celebration August-September at Siddhivinayak Temple for five days with elaborate rituals and ceremonies.
significance: Ashtavinayak pilgrimage festival; temple legend associates Vishnu's penance where Ganesha bestowed divine powers.

name: Anganewadi Jatra (Bharadi Devi Yatra)
description: Major annual fair at Bharadi Devi Temple in Anganewadi village (Masure, ~10-12 km from Malvan). Goddess Bharadi (Earth Goddess) renowned for wish-fulfilling power. Festival February or March with no fixed date (decided by consensus). Rituals 4am to 10pm with mass cooking and 'Taate Lawane' (prasad serving). Devotees from Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka participate.
significance: Known as 'Pandharpur of Konkan'; one of biggest religious events in region; goddess legend spans 400 years.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: Celebrated August-September at Chintamani Temple for 10 days with temple ceremonies and processions honoring Chintamani Vinayaka.
significance: Ashtavinayak festival; temple associated with Ganapatya saint Morya Gosavi; renovated by Peshwa Madhavrao I.

name: Maghi Chaturthi
description: Festival January-February at Chintamani Temple from Chaturthi to Ashtami with temple rituals and celebrations.
significance: Ashtavinayak festival period; temple at sacred Sangam (confluence) of Mula, Mutha, and Bhima rivers.

name: Maha Shivaratri
description: Most important festival for Shiva devotees at Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga Temple. Midnight Nishita Kaal puja draws massive crowds.
significance: Festival honoring Shiva; temple is ancient Shaiva Akhada center; one of 12 sacred Jyotirlingas.

name: Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Kumbh Mela
description: Held every 12 years when Jupiter is in Leo. One of four traditional Kumbha Melas. Dual centers: Ramkund (Panchavati, Vaishnava) and Kushavarta (Trimbakeshwar, Shaiva). Single dip during Shahi Snan (royal bath) believed to grant Moksha.
significance: One of four major Hindu pilgrimage Melas; occurs every 12 years; draws millions; next mela October 2026 to July 2028 with peak rituals in 2027.

name: Maha Shivaratri
description: Night-long festival celebrating Lord Shiva at Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga. Marked by elaborate abhishek (ritual bathing), chanting of Vedic hymns, grand processions, and massive influx of pilgrims offering bilva leaves and holy water to the lingam. Bhasma Aarti slots sell out months in advance.
significance: Religious—dedicated to Lord Shiva; one of twelve sacred Jyotirlingas; lakhs of devotees participate

name: Simhastha Kumbh Mela
approximate_date: April-May (every 12 years; next in 2028: 27 March–27 May)
description: One of four major Kumbh Melas in India, held in Ujjain when Jupiter enters Leo (Simha Rashi). Spans two months with three main Shahi Snan (sacred bathing) dates where hundreds of thousands of sadhus and pilgrims participate in grand processions and holy dips in the Shipra River, believed to cleanse the soul and lead to moksha.
significance: Spiritual—one of Hinduism's holiest pilgrimages; major gathering of sadhus and ascetics; astronomically timed event

name: Maha Shivaratri
description: Festival at Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga on the Om-shaped island in the Narmada River. Marked by night-long abhishek, Vedic chanting, grand processions, and pilgrims offering prayers to Lord Shiva at this sacred Jyotirlinga.
significance: Religious—one of twelve Jyotirlingas; pilgrimage site on sacred Narmada River

name: Kartik Purnima
description: Ten-day festival at Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga celebrated at the end of Chaturmas. A major fair is organized where devotees take holy dips in the Narmada River and offer prayers to Lord Shiva, making it a spiritually enriching experience for thousands of pilgrims.
significance: Religious—sacred bathing festival; honors end of monsoon season (Chaturmas)

name: Tansen Samaroh
description: Annual music festival held near the tomb of Tansen in Behat village, Gwalior, honoring the legendary musician Sangeet Shiromani Tansen. Features performances by world-class vocal and instrumental artists, awards ceremony with National Tansen Samman and Raja Mansingh Tomar Samman presentations on the opening day. Celebrates classical Indian music legacy.
significance: Cultural—tribute to India's greatest musician; world-renowned classical music festival

name: Mandu Festival
description: Five-day cultural and heritage festival showcasing Mandu's Afghan-era architecture and local traditions. Features adventure sports, cycling expeditions, live music concerts, local art and craft exhibitions, food stalls, poetry readings, nature trails, and architecture-themed activities celebrating the region's rich cultural heritage.
significance: Cultural—celebrates regional heritage and architecture; promotes tourism and local traditions

name: Nagdwari Mela
description: Festival celebrated in Pachmarhi dedicated to the worship of Nag Devata (serpent deity). Attracts thousands of tourists from Nagpur and Maharashtra who visit the fair to worship the serpent deity. Historically held during Nag Panchami (July-August), the festival timing has shifted to November in recent years.
significance: Religious—worship of Nag Devata; significant for Maharashtra and Nagpur communities

name: Buddha Purnima
description: Festival at Sanchi Buddhist stupa celebrating Buddha's birth, enlightenment, and passing on the full moon day of Vaishakh month. Attracts monks and followers from Bhutan, China, Japan, Cambodia, and Sri Lanka who gather at this UNESCO World Heritage Site. District administration ensures comprehensive arrangements including security, cleanliness, water, and health facilities.
significance: Religious—celebrates three events in Buddha's life; gathers international Buddhist community

name: Lokrang Festival
description: One of India's most anticipated cultural celebrations honoring tribal and folk traditions through music, dance, art, storytelling, and local cuisine. Held at Ravindra Bhavan Complex with performances, exhibitions, and cultural experiences reflecting rural and indigenous Indian heritage. Free admission. Running for over two decades.
significance: Cultural—celebration of tribal and folk heritage; largest festival in Madhya Pradesh for tribal culture

name: Vel Vel Festival
description: Also known as the Fire Walking Festival, this unique celebration showcases the syncretic traditions of the Moreh border town, drawing participation from Tamils, Meiteis, Burmese, and other communities. The festival traditionally features a fire-walking ceremony (barefoot walking over burning coal) as its defining ritual, though this was suspended after 2024 due to ethnic tensions.
significance: Symbolizes communal harmony and cultural diversity at the Indo-Myanmar border.

name: Gaan-Ngai
description: The New Year and post-harvest festival of the Zeliangrong people (Zeme, Rongmei, Liangmai, Inpui tribes). Gaan-Ngai lasts five days and marks the closing of the old year and arrival of the new one. The festival carries hopes for peace and prosperity.
significance: Greatest and most important festival of the Zeliangrong Nagas; celebrates the dry winter season after harvest with traditional dances and rituals.

name: Orange Festival
description: Annual state-level festival celebrating Tamenglong's position as Manipur's largest orange producer. The festival features over 300 orange growers and exhibitors competing for prizes, with the winning orange receiving Rs 2,00,000. Cultural activities include traditional dances, tug-of-war, indigenous wrestling, traditional fire-making show, and folk song presentations.
significance: Promotes the largest produced fruit of the district and showcases local agricultural heritage and culture.

name: Shirui Lily Festival
approximate_date: Last week of May through second week of June
description: Five-day cultural and ecological festival celebrating the delicate and endangered Lilium Mackliniae, which blooms only in the Shirui Hills of Ukhrul. The festival honors Manipur's state flower (declared in 1989) and showcases Tangkhul Naga culture. Activities include a Shirui Lily Literature Festival, trash collection marathon, traditional weaving exhibitions, SheChef cooking competition, drone light shows, and the Miss Shirui Lily pageant.
significance: Celebrates biodiversity, Tangkhul Naga heritage, and Ukhrul as Manipur's highest hill station. The Shirui Lily is an endangered endemic species found nowhere else on Earth.

name: Luira Phanit
approximate_date: February 15 (Lui-Ngai-Ni, the universal Naga date), also celebrated Jan-Mar depending on village traditions
description: The New Year and seed-sowing festival of the Tangkhul Naga tribe, marking the onset of the agricultural season. Luira Phanit (from 'Lui' = field, 'ra' = dig, 'phanit' = festival) invokes the Almighty's blessings for crops and prosperity. The festival features indigenous games, music, dance, folk performances, and the significant Luithui Khami ritual where the Awunga (chief) and Awungva (chief queen) perform the first seed-sowing, after which villagers are permitted to sow their own seeds.
significance: Significant cultural and agricultural ritual for the Tangkhul Naga; marks the opening of the new farming year with ceremonial blessings.

name: Monolith Festival
approximate_date: Variable (October and March observed; timing differs by year)
description: Three-day festival held at Mawphlang Sacred Groves celebrating Khasi heritage, culture, and the ancient stone monoliths ('mawbynnas') that mark spiritual points in the forest. The festival features soulful and mesmerizing music, traditional Khasi rituals, and cultural performances. The Mawphlang Sacred Forest itself dates back over 800 years and is the oldest and largest sacred forest for the Khasi tribes.
significance: Celebrates Khasi tribal heritage and the sacred forest's deep spiritual and cultural significance. Showcases the community's ritual traditions and connection to the ancient sacred landscape.

name: Hnahsin Kut (Cosmos Festival)
description: An eco-tourism festival celebrating the blooming of the native cosmos flower (hnahsin) in Champhai. The festival transforms the region into a sea of pinks, purples, and whites, featuring flower exhibitions, paragliding, cultural performances, artisan markets, and traditional food stalls showcasing Mizo culture and handicrafts.
significance: Celebrates Champhai's natural beauty and botanical heritage; promotes eco-tourism and local artisan economy

name: Leitlangpui Music Festival
description: A three-day music and cultural festival held in Lunglei celebrating Mizo art, culture, and music. Features the Leitlangpui Band Contest, Hathkargha Mela State Handloom Expo, traditional musical and cultural performances, and opportunities to experience local entrepreneurship and tourism promotion.
significance: Celebrates Mizo music and cultural heritage; bridges local culture with tourism development

name: Dzukou Valley Festival
description: An inaugural festival celebrating the pristine natural beauty of Dzukou Valley at the Nagaland-Manipur border. Features camping, trekking, evening bonfire gatherings with local musicians, valley exploration, and starry-night experiences amidst the valley's rolling green meadows and the rare Dzukou Lily bloom.
significance: Celebrates the region's untouched natural landscape and biodiversity; promotes responsible tourism to a sensitive ecosystem

name: Sekrenyi
description: A ten-day purification festival of the Angami Naga people held in Khonoma and surrounding Angami villages. The festival involves ceremonial cleansing of the body and soul to wash away past sins, renewal rituals, initiation of young people to adulthood, and community unification. Represents an identity marker of the Angami people with deep spiritual and social significance.
significance: Religious and cultural identity festival of Angami Nagas; marks the purification and renewal of the community; ritual initiation into adulthood

name: Mongmong Festival
description: A six-day harvest festival celebrated by the Sangtam Naga tribe in Kiphire. Mongmong means 'Togetherness Forever' and involves various rituals, traditional dances, feasts, and thanksgiving ceremonies to honor the gods for a bountiful harvest of crops.
significance: Harvest celebration and thanksgiving festival of the Sangtam people; reinforces community unity and agricultural traditions

name: Metemneo Festival
description: A five-day harvest festival celebrated by the Yimchunger Naga tribe in Kiphire after the millet crop harvest. Features traditional rituals praying for the souls of the departed, traditional dances, and young people engagement ceremonies, reflecting the community's spiritual and social bonds.
significance: Harvest and spiritual renewal festival of the Yimchunger people; honors the departed and marks life transitions

name: Tsükhenye Festival
description: A four-day harvest festival celebrated by the Chakhesang Naga tribe in Pfutsero to mark the successful harvest year and rejuvenate the community. The festival begins with a sacred purification ceremony involving the village priest's sacrificial offering, followed by merrymaking, traditional dances, sports, games, and leisure activities that reinforce community bonds.
significance: Harvest celebration and purification festival of the Chakhesang people; marks agricultural cycle completion and community renewal

name: Orange and Tourism Festival
description: An annual celebration held at Jampui Hills to honor the successful orange harvest. Features orange picking, cultural performances by local communities, traditional food stalls, grand fair with handicraft exhibitions (Tibetan crafts, handlooms), tea and coffee sales, and arrangement of oranges in sculptural patterns depicting wildlife and Indian monuments. Also offers adventure sports including paragliding, trekking, cycling, and zip-lining.
significance: Celebrates Jampui's renowned orange cultivation and agricultural heritage; promotes tourism and showcases tribal craftsmanship

name: Neermahal Water Festival - Boat Race
description: An annual water festival held on Rudrasagar Lake featuring thrilling boat races with vibrantly decorated traditional boats. Teams row in unison in competitive races, with approximately 10 boats competing simultaneously. The festival also includes swimming competitions and cultural performances, drawing crowds to celebrate the region's aquatic heritage against the backdrop of the Neermahal water palace.
significance: Celebrates Tripura's water heritage and aquatic traditions; showcases community spirit and tribal craftsmanship in boat-building

name: Ashokastami Mela
description: An annual pilgrimage fair held at the rock-cut Shaiva shrine of Unakoti attracting tens of thousands of devotees. The primary ritual centers on taking a holy dip at Ashtamikunda, considered highly auspicious for good fortune. The festival features music performances, traditional folk dance, cultural celebrations, and local food stalls. Devotees from various religions and castes congregate to honor the sacred site and its ancient rock-cut sculptures.
significance: Major pilgrimage festival of Shaivite Hinduism; celebrates the UNESCO-tentative-listed rock-cut heritage (7th-9th century CE); brings together diverse communities for spiritual celebration

name: Dhauli Kalinga Mahotsav
description: Classical, folk, and martial dance festival held at the Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) on Dhauli Hill. Features performances from classical dance forms and the distinctive Odissi and martial traditions, organized jointly by Odisha Culture & Tourism and Odisha Dance Academy.
significance: Celebrates the artistic heritage at one of Odisha's five major Buddhist sites, the location of Emperor Ashoka's spiritual awakening after the Kalinga War.

name: Buddha Purnima
description: Major Buddhist pilgrimage at Dhauli Shanti Stupa marking the birth, enlightenment, and death of Gautama Buddha. Buddhists from across India and the world gather to pay respects at this sacred location.
significance: Celebrates Buddha's spiritual achievements at the location where Emperor Ashoka transformed from a warrior to a peaceful leader after witnessing the devastation of the Kalinga War.

name: Nrusingha Chaturdasi (Baisakh Mela)
description: Annual fair and pilgrimage event at Nrusinghanath Temple on the Gandhamardan hills, celebrating the divine incarnation of Lord Nrusimhanath. Attracts thousands of pilgrims from across Odisha and neighboring states. Pilgrims trek the 16 km connection between the twin temples (Nrusinghanath in Bargarh and Harishankar in Balangir).
significance: Commemorates the avatar of Lord Nrusimhanath (rare Vidala-Nrusimha form with cat's head and lion's body). One of the principal annual festivals at this sacred site.

name: Chandipur Beach Festival
description: Four-day Golden Beach Festival celebrating Odisha's coastal culture through traditional music, classical and folk dance (Chhau, Kathak, Bharatnatyam, Odissi), handicraft exhibitions, and local sports. Features performances by local and national artists.
significance: Showcases regional artistic traditions and crafts at the unique vanishing-tide beach where the sea recedes up to 5 km during ebb tide.

name: Gopalpur Beach Festival
description: Four-day coastal celebration blending tradition, culture, and modernity at this historic beach in Ganjam district. Features the first-ever Sea Aarti ceremony performed by Varanasi saints, torch processions from local temples, Star Nights with Bollywood and Odissi performances, traditional dances (Sambalpuri, Kuchipudi, Ghumura), and Pallishree Mela with 250+ handicraft and food stalls.
significance: Positions Gopalpur as a global coastal tourism destination while highlighting Odisha's ancient maritime heritage and cultural significance. Celebrates the merging of history with the present.

name: Chaitra Mela
description: Annual pilgrimage festival held in the nearby village of Chandaneswar featuring worship at the ancient Shiva temple during the Hindu month of Chaitra. Thousands of devotees gather for ritual worship and fair celebrations.
significance: One of the principal annual fairs in the region, blending spiritual observance with community gathering at the sacred Shiva temple associated with Talasari area.

name: Dubdi Monastery Festival
approximate_date: February (15th day of 1st Tibetan lunar month)
description: Annual festival at Dubdi Monastery, the oldest monastery in Sikkim (established 1701), located above Yuksom. Features Buddhist rituals and celebrations marking the Buddhist calendar with prayers performed by monks.
significance: Oldest monastery in Sikkim; celebrates Tibetan Buddhist traditions

name: Pang Lhabsol
approximate_date: Late August / Early September (15th day of 7th Tibetan lunar month)
description: Festival honoring Mount Khangchendzonga, the guardian deity of Sikkim. Celebrated at Samdruptse Monastery in Namchi with masked Cham dances, religious ceremonies, and fireworks. Commemorates the consecration of Khangchendzonga and the Treaty of brotherhood among Lepchas and Bhutias.
significance: Major Sikkim festival honoring the state's guardian deity; celebrates inter-community harmony

name: Tendong Lho Rum Faat
approximate_date: August (3rd month of Tibetan lunar calendar; typically early August)
description: Lepcha festival commemorating Mount Tendong's protection of ancestors during 40 days of continuous rain. Grand celebrations held in Namchi with a trek from Ravangla/Damthang up Tendong Hill, cultural performances, and local cuisine.
significance: Lepcha tribal festival celebrating sacred mountain protection and cultural heritage

name: Mahakala Dance (Ralang Monastery)
description: Annual masked dance performance at nearby Ralang Monastery celebrating the deity Mahakala. Part of Tibetan Buddhist festival traditions.
significance: Tibetan Buddhist ritual dance honoring protective deities

name: Sani Peyarchi (Saturn Transit Festival)
description: Major festival at Tirunallar Saniswaran Temple honoring Saturn (Shani). Features special abhishekams (ritual ablutions), homams (fire sacrifices), and poojas dedicated to Lord Saneeswaran. Thousands of devotees arrive to observe Saturn's transit.
significance: Major Hindu festival celebrating Saturn transitions; significant astrological observance in South Indian tradition

name: Baisakhi
description: Grand annual fair at Takht Sri Damdama Sahib (Talwandi Sabo) celebrating Baisakhi—the Sikh new year and harvest festival. Commemorates the foundation day of the Khalsa Panth (1699). Features colorful decorations, devotee gatherings, stalls selling traditional prashaad, sweets, and trinkets. Major pilgrimage site where Guru Gobind Singh compiled the Adi Granth.
significance: Major Sikh festival marking Khalsa founding; significant pilgrimage and harvest celebration

name: Sharan Navaratri at Jogulamba Temple
description: Nine-day festival honoring Goddess Jogulamba with special pujas, rituals, and cultural programs. Features Kalyanotsavam (temple marriage ceremony), Chariot Festival (Ratha Yatra), Nadi Aarti, and Teppotsavam (boat ritual). One of the only Shakti Peeth temples in Telangana.
significance: Major religious festival at principal Shakti Peeth shrine; draws thousands of devotees across Sept-Oct

name: Karthika Pournami Jatara
description: Annual fair held for 11 days including Karthika Pournami (full moon in Karthika month). Marks sacred observance at Anantha Padmanabha Swamy temple with rituals and pilgrim gatherings.
significance: Major pilgrimage fair at ancient Vishnu temple; one of two annual jataras

name: Ashada Jatara
description: Five-day fair held at Anantha Padmanabha Swamy temple during Ashada month. Second annual jatara with pilgrim participation and ritual observances.
significance: Secondary pilgrimage fair at temple; monsoon-season gathering

name: Braj Holi Festival
description: Two-day festival celebrated at Deeg Palace with great pomp, honoring Lord Krishna and Braj region heritage. Features colorful fountain displays (900 fountains operational), Rajasthani folk performances, kabaddi, rope pulling, Mehendi art, and rangoli competitions.
significance: Major Krishna-linked festival in Braj belt; iconic palace fountain spectacle; state-level celebration

name: Mitthe Shah Dargah Urs Fair
description: Annual colorful fair held at the mausoleum of Sufi Saint Mitthe Shah, located just outside Gagron Fort. Features music, rituals, and traditional communal gatherings celebrating the intersection of regional faith, folklore, and harmony.
significance: Sacred Sufi shrine festival; demonstrates syncretic religious traditions within UNESCO World Heritage fort complex

name: Kumbhalgarh Festival
description: Three-day cultural festival held at Kumbhalgarh Fort organized by Rajasthan Tourism Department. Features folk music and dance (Sufi, Kalbelia, Bhavai, Chari, Ghoomar), sound-and-light show narrating fort history, traditional Rajasthani handicrafts markets (haats), and celebrations of Maharana Kumbha's legacy.
significance: State-level heritage festival celebrating 15th-century fort and Mewar dynasty; major cultural celebration during prime tourism season

name: Mahavir Jayanti
description: Celebrates the birthday of Mahavir, founder of Jainism. Major festival at 15th-century Ranakpur Jain Temple with 1,000+ daily visitors (15,000 during festival). Temple idol adorned with silver crowns; 1,000 kilos of rice offered annually.
significance: Principal Jain pilgrimage festival; one of most important observances at temple; major religious celebration attracting devotees nationwide

name: Hanuman Jayanti
description: Grand fair organized at Pandupol Hanuman Temple within Sariska Tiger Reserve celebrating the birth of Lord Hanuman. Draws pilgrims and locals for rituals, prayers, and festive gatherings at the 5,000-year-old shrine.
significance: Annual pilgrimage fair at sacred temple within wildlife reserve; celebrates Hindu mythology and devotion

name: Vaikasi Brahmotsavam (Garuda Sevai)
description: Annual 10-day Brahmotsavam festival at Varadaraja Perumal Temple, with the spectacular Garuda Sevai procession on the third day where the deity is carried on the golden Garuda vahanam. The seventh day features the chariot (ther) festival through the streets of Kanchipuram.
significance: Major temple festival; religious significance to Vaishnavism; draws thousands of devotees from across Tamil Nadu

name: Thaipusam
description: Major 10-day festival at Arulmigu Dandayudhapani Murugan Temple on the hill. Thaipusam attracts approximately 300,000 devotees who undertake pilgrimages to the hilltop temple and undergo religious rituals and offerings.
significance: Hindu religious festival; pilgrimage; major festival at this six-abode Murugan shrine; deeply significant to Murugan devotees across South India

name: Panguni Uthiram
description: Ten-day major festival at Palani Murugan Temple marking the celestial marriage of Lord Muruga with Devasena. Estimated 500,000+ devotees ascend the hill for darshan and religious celebrations at one of the six sacred Murugan abodes.
significance: One of the most significant Murugan temple festivals in South India; religious pilgrimage; widely celebrated across Tamil temples

name: Kodai Vizha (Summer Festival and Flower Show)
description: Major annual summer festival hosted by Tamil Nadu Tourism Department at Kodaikanal hill station. Features elaborate flower structures planted with over 2.5 lakh seedlings, vegetable carvings, boat races on Kodai Lake, dog shows, and cultural folk dances at Bryant Park.
significance: Major hill station cultural event; attracts thousands of visitors nationwide; showcases horticultural excellence

name: Coonoor Fruit Show (Nilgiris Summer Festival)
approximate_date: May (typically May 24-26; as part of Nilgiris Summer Festival)
description: Annual fruit exhibition at Sim's Park, Coonoor featuring colourful display of fruits sourced from across India, artistically arranged. Part of the broader Nilgiris Summer Festival celebrated across Ooty, Coonoor, Kotagiri, and Gudalur in May.
significance: Regional horticultural event; showcases local produce and agricultural heritage of the Nilgiris

name: Arudra Darshan (Margazhi Tiruvadhirai)
description: Main annual festival at Perur Patteeswarar Temple (Shiva temple in Coimbatore). The temple is known as 'Melai Chidambaram' or Chidambaram of the West, and this festival celebrates an important aspect of Lord Shiva.
significance: Major temple festival; religious significance; temple revered as second to Chidambaram among Shiva temples

name: Panguni Brahmotsavam
description: Annual festival at Perur Patteeswarar Temple featuring temple chariot procession through the surrounding neighbourhood, with traditional religious ceremonies and rituals.
significance: Major temple festival; chariot festival tradition

name: Skanda Sashti
description: Six-day festival at Arulmigu Solaimalai (Pazhamudircholai) Murugan Temple, one of the six sacred abodes of Lord Muruga. Celebrates Muruga's victory over evil forces with traditional religious observances.
significance: Major Murugan festival; religious and cultural significance; pilgrimage site

name: Panguni Uthiram
description: Festival at Pazhamudircholai Murugan Temple (one of six sacred Murugan abodes) celebrating the celestial marriage of Lord Muruga. Major pilgrimage occasion at this temple.
significance: Religious festival; pilgrimage; significant to Murugan devotees

name: Karthigai Deepam
approximate_date: November-December (10-day Brahmotsavam; Maha Deepam on final day)
description: The Festival of Lamps at Arunachaleswarar Temple. The ten-day Karthigai Brahmotsavam culminates with the Bharani Deepam (sacred lamp) lit at the temple, followed by the Mahadeepam (Great Lamp) ignited atop Annamalai Hill. Lakhs of devotees gather for the final night, witnessing the giant beacon signifying Shiva's manifestation as the element of fire.
significance: One of Tamil Nadu's most significant temple festivals. The Maha Deepam on the hilltop is visible from miles around and marks the pinnacle of this major pilgrimage event.

name: Skanda Sashti
description: Celebrated over six days at the seashore Murugan temple. Commemorates Lord Murugan's victory over the demon Surapadma. The climax on the sixth day (Sashti) features the Soorasamharam—a dramatic re-enactment of the celestial battle on the seashore, with Murugan's defeat of Surapadman's various manifestations. Tiruchendur is the canonical venue for this festival across Tamil Nadu, drawing hundreds of thousands on the final day.
significance: The most heavily attended Soorasamharam celebration in Tamil Nadu, held at the only Murugan shrine among the six abodes that sits directly on the coast.

name: Thaipusam
description: Celebrates Lord Murugan's birthday and the day he received the divine spear (Vel) from Goddess Parvati. Devotees participate in elaborate rituals including ceremonial bathing of the deity and carrying kavadis (wooden frameworks) as offerings. Marked by processions and devoted worship.
significance: Major festival at this Arupadai Veedu (one of six sacred Murugan abodes), celebrating Murugan's divine power and the bond between mother and son.

name: Skanda Sashti
description: Six-day festival commemorating Lord Murugan's victory over evil forces. Celebrated with grand rituals, Soorasamharam re-enactments, devotional music, fasting, and processions. The festival demonstrates Murugan's supreme power and his role as destroyer of evil.
significance: Major annual celebration at Swamimalai Swaminathaswamy Temple with specific rituals, processions, and performances drawing devotees throughout the region.

name: Vaikasi Vishakham / Brahmotsavam
description: Fourteen-day Brahmotsavam celebrated during Vaikasi Vishakham, commemorating Lord Murugan's birth star (Vishakha nakshatra). The festival culminates in the Car Festival, a grand procession displaying the deity on elaborate mounts. Murugan is celebrated as the presiding power during this period.
significance: Major annual festival at this Arupadai Veedu, marking Murugan's birth and drawing large devotee participation with elaborate ritual ceremonies.

name: Panguni Uthiram
description: Major festival celebrated with great pomp. Brahmotsavam conducted in the month of Panguni features processions where deities are carried through the temple. This festival celebrates the divine marriage and is observed with elaborate rituals and public participation.
significance: One of the principal festivals at Tiruparankundram, attracting significant pilgrimage traffic and marked by grand ceremonial processions.

name: Thaipusam
description: Commemorates Lord Murugan receiving the divine spear (Vel) from his mother, Goddess Parvati. Celebrated at the hilltop Arupadai Veedu with beautiful temple decorations, grand processions, rituals, and masses of devotees undertaking the pilgrimage.
significance: Major festival at Thiruthani drawing large crowds; celebrates Murugan's strength and the devotional bond between mother and son.

name: Skanda Sashti
description: Six-day festival celebrating Lord Murugan's victory over demon Surapadman. Observed with great fervor at Thiruthani with elaborate temple decorations, grand processions, rituals, and fasting. Draws large crowds throughout the six-day period.
significance: Principal festival at this Arupadai Veedu, commemorating Murugan's triumph and spiritual significance across the region.

name: Vaikunta Ekadasi
description: Grand 21-day festival at Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple in Srirangam. The festival is divided into two parts: Pagal Pathu (10 days before Ekadashi) and Ira Pathu (10 days after). On the main Ekadashi day, elaborate rituals commence at 3 AM. The deity is adorned with bejewelled armor and proceeds to the Swarga Vaasal (Gate to Vaikuntha), where the temple doors are ceremonially opened, followed by a procession to the 1000-Pillared Mandapam.
significance: Considered the height of all spiritual festivals observed in Trichy. This iconic 21-day celebration is one of the grandest temple festivals in South India.

name: Samayapuram Mariamman Brahmotsavam
description: Annual Brahmotsavam celebrated at Samayapuram Mariamman Temple, located 17 km from Trichy. Thousands of devotees from various castes and communities gather to worship Goddess Mariamman during this major festival celebrating her divine power and blessings.
significance: Principal annual festival at this famous pilgrimage centre, drawing diverse communities and demonstrating the goddess's universal appeal.

name: Summer Festival
description: Annual celebration held during mid-May coinciding with the festival of Lord Servarayan (Shevaroy), the presiding deity of the Shevaroy Hills. Features a 7-day exhibition including spectacular Flower Shows with thousands of potted flowering plants, dog shows, boating races, and village fairs. Traditional performances include Karakattam (an ancient Tamil folk dance) and Naiyandi Melam (percussion performances).
significance: Major seasonal draw for the hill station celebrating local heritage, flora, and culture. Most tourists visit Yercaud during May specifically for this festival.

name: Holi (Festival of Colours)
description: Holi celebrates the love between Krishna and Radha, central to Mathura and Braj region culture. The festival lasts a week, with Lathmar Holi at Barsana and Nandgaon featuring women playfully hitting men with sticks (symbolising Krishna's village pranks). Mathura's celebrations include colour throwing, bonfires (Holika Dahan), Dahi Handi (breaking pots of curd/butter), and Ras Leela dances depicting Krishna and Radha's love story.
significance: Mathura is Krishna's birthplace, making Holi a deeply spiritual festival tied to his divine leela (divine play). The Braj region is the iconic heart of Holi celebrations in India, drawing hundreds of thousands of pilgrims annually.

name: Krishna Janmashtami (Birth of Krishna)
description: Janmashtami celebrates Lord Krishna's birth in Mathura at midnight. Over 800,000 devotees gather annually for prayers, fasting, and Dahi Handi competitions where youth form human pyramids to break pots of curd and butter. Ras Leela performances, temple decorations, midnight aarti (worship ceremonies), and distribution of sweets mark the festival. Vrindavan celebrations extend for 16 days.
significance: Mathura is Krishna's birthplace (Krishna Janma Bhoomi temple), making this the most sacred site for Janmashtami celebrations in India. The festival is central to Hindu devotional practice and Braj culture.

name: Durga Puja
approximate_date: September-October (lunar calendar; 2026: late September / early October)
description: UNESCO-inscribed Intangible Cultural Heritage festival celebrating the victory of Goddess Durga over evil. Kolkata hosts thousands of elaborate pandals (temporary structures), cultural performances, Dhunuchi Naach (incense stick dances), food stalls, and processions. The festival lasts 10 days, with the final five (Shashti to Vijaya Dashami) being most prominent. In 2022, the collective economy was ₹50,000 crores, employing three lakh people.
significance: Durga Puja is the largest, most iconic festival in Kolkata, deeply embedded in Bengali identity and spiritual practice. Recognised by UNESCO (December 2021) for its cultural significance.

name: Kali Puja
approximate_date: November (new moon day of Kartika month; 2026: November 8)
